D005-D015_h001.question:
It’s hard to explain, but for the last couple of months I’ve felt like something’s really off with me.

I drive the city bus on the early shift, and lately I’ve had this strong sense that I’m… meant for more than this. Not just in a “daydreaming” way. It feels almost like I’ve been chosen for some special role, like I’m supposed to be noticed by important people, maybe even involved in some bigger plan. I catch myself thinking that the cameras on the bus or the traffic lights are somehow tracking me because I’m important, like they’re watching to see what I’ll do.

Around the same time, I started smelling things that no one else seems to notice. Sometimes it’s this strong burning or chemical smell, other times like rotten food, even when the bus is clean and the passengers say they don’t smell anything. It can happen at home too, when my wife doesn’t notice anything.

I’ve been more down and tired than usual, not enjoying stuff I used to, but I’m not sure if that’s because of all this or something else. I just know this has been going on for about two months and it’s really worrying me.

    B. Schizophrenia

    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

I’m sure there’s a terrible smell coming from me, like something spoiled, even when the nurses say they don’t notice anything.

Sometimes I smell smoke or chemicals in my room when no one else does. I call the nurse to check, and she says there’s nothing burning, but it seems so real that I get scared we’ll all catch fire.

I’ve also been… acting strangely, I suppose. I catch myself giggling or humming little songs at the wrong times, like during meals or when someone is talking about something serious. The staff tell me to calm down, but it just slips out.

Along with all that, I’ve been feeling very low. I don’t have much interest in the activities here anymore. I stay in my room, feel tired all the time, and sometimes I wonder what the point of anything is now that my husband is gone.

It’s been about three months now that things have really felt off. I’m still working—showings, open houses, dealing with inspectors—but it’s getting harder to keep it together.

I’ve started to feel like people are watching me, not just clients, but like there’s some group keeping tabs on where I go. When I’m driving between listings, I catch myself checking the rearview mirror over and over, convinced the same car is following me. At the office, I sometimes think the security cameras aren’t just for the building, but specifically aimed at me.

I also hear this voice sometimes—usually when I’m alone in my car or at home at night. It’s not like my own thoughts; it sounds like someone standing behind me, commenting on what I’m doing, sometimes criticizing me. I know it doesn’t really make sense, but in the moment it feels very real.

On top of that, I’ve been low for a while—dragging myself out of bed, no energy, not really enjoying closing deals like I used to. My hands or feet will start doing this little repetitive tapping or rubbing, almost like a nervous habit I can’t stop once it starts. It all makes it hard to feel like myself.

I’ve also noticed I’ll catch myself repeating these little movements—tapping my fingers in a certain pattern, rocking my foot back and forth—for no real reason, and it’s hard to stop once I start.
